value.body: A transport planner studies how people and goods move through a city or region and plans the roads, public transport, walking and cycling networks that serve them. Employers include transport and infrastructure consultancies, metro and city transport bodies, and research groups. Work involves traffic surveys, data analysis, modelling and writing project reports.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Plan, or B.Tech Civil followed by an M.Plan / M.Tech in transport

items.label: Operational metro rail network
items.note: Across 26 cities, incl. 55 km Delhi–Meerut RRTS; up from ~248 km in 2014
items.source: PIB (Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join transport or infrastructure consultancies as junior planners or analysts working on mobility plans, metro and bus studies, and road projects. A master's in transport planning or engineering is common for modelling-heavy roles.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Data analysis in Excel and GIS

value.title: At a glance
items: Much work comes from metro, bus and city mobility projects.
Modelling and data skills are increasingly asked for.
Next roles: senior transport planner, project lead, mobility specialist.

competition.note: B.Plan graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
